The whole picture first, then we build it from the bottom. Governance on top, projections above the log, disposable compute below. The log is the recorded truth; everything else is derived or replaceable.

One log, everything derived

Four bands. Governance on top of every read and every tool call. Three families of projections. The log in the middle: messages, tasks, tool calls, results, corrections. Compute below, all of it disposable. It grows incrementally: a projection per new read pattern, a worker class per new execution pattern, the durable history underneath. Said, not shown: The log records truth. Projections are derived. Compute is disposable. External systems stay the source of truth for the facts they own.
The share consumer in six lines. Records are leased, not assigned; each one is acknowledged on its own: ACCEPT when the tool ran, RELEASE so another worker retries, REJECT for poison. One detail worth saying: a share group refuses auto.offset.reset, the start position is a group config on the broker.

Lease, ack, release

ShareGroup.java · Kafka 4.3var props = Kafka.consumer(group); props.remove("auto.offset.reset"); // the broker decides where to start props.put("share.acknowledgement.mode", "explicit"); // we acknowledge per record try (var worker = new KafkaShareConsumer<String, String>(props)) { worker.subscribe(List.of(topic)); while (done < 5) { for (var rec : worker.poll(Duration.ofSeconds(1))) { // leased, not owned try { run(rec.value()); // slow, non-deterministic worker.acknowledge(rec, AcknowledgeType.ACCEPT); // done done++; } catch (RuntimeException transientFailure) { worker.acknowledge(rec, AcknowledgeType.RELEASE); // someone else retries } } worker.commitSync(); // flush the acks } }
Run against Kafka 4.3.0: five jobs, one transient failure released and redelivered, five acknowledged. share.acknowledgement.mode=explicit is what makes the per-record decision ours; implicit mode acknowledges on the next poll. The broker-side start position: kafka-configs --entity-type groups --add-config share.auto.offset.reset=earliest.
What a learned decision looks like on the wire: a bounded question in, a typed answer with probabilities out. No free text to parse. This is what a router or a triage step should call.

Typed in, typed out

POST /v1/systemone { "state": "fan 100 %, VPN down", "model": "jev-latest", "questions": { "route": { "type": "choice", "criteria": [ "windows", "network", "macos" ] } } }
200 OK { "model": "jev-1.13.0", "answers": { "route": { "choice": "windows", "probabilities": { "windows": 0.91, "network": 0.06, "macos": 0.03 }, "confidence": 0.91 } } }
What a learned decision looks like on the wire. State is the text or JSON to judge; questions are typed: noul for a yes/no probability, choice for one option among yours, score for an ordered level. The answer is constrained to the options you supplied, with probabilities and a confidence; no free text to parse. This is the call a router or a triage step makes instead of a generative prompt. Endpoint POST api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone; the case and the probabilities are illustrative, the schema is TypeSafe AI's documented System One API. Note: the real request writes criteria as an object of option → description; the array here is a shorthand for the slide.
